Meniscus Centralization Reviewer

A blinded, cross-sectional case review of 30 meniscus root repairs.

How this works
  1. 1

    Enter your name below to begin the review.

  2. 2

    Review a short set of definitions, then tell us your preferred centralization technique.This is asked once and is saved on this device, linked to your profile, for next time.

  3. 3

    Review each clinical vignette and the representative imaging.Each vignette includes age, BMI, tear chronicity, mechanical alignment, medial compartment Outerbridge grade, and meniscal extrusion measurements.

  4. 4

    For each case, select the single approach you would take.Centralization, Capsulodesis, Osteotomy/Mechanical Correction, No Repair/Non-Surgical, or Other (with a short description).

  5. 5

    Complete all 30 cases based on your independent clinical judgment.

  6. 6

    Your responses are saved automatically in your browser and submitted as you go.You may close the survey and return later using the same browser and device.

  7. 7

    At any point, click Download PDF to save a PDF summary of your answers so far — useful to keep as a backup or for your own records.

Used only to save your progress — never shown to other reviewers.

Before You Begin

A quick refresher on the terms used throughout this review.

Key definitions
  1. 1

    Absolute extrusionThe distance, in millimeters, that the meniscal body protrudes beyond the tibial plateau margin, measured on coronal MRI.

  2. 2

    Relative extrusionAbsolute extrusion expressed as a percentage of total meniscal width (absolute extrusion ÷ meniscal width). This normalizes for meniscus size across patients.

  3. 3

    Meniscus centralizationA technique that anchors the meniscocapsular junction or meniscal body directly to the tibial plateau — typically with a suture anchor or transosseous tunnel — to reduce extrusion and restore hoop tension, usually performed at the time of root repair.

  4. 4

    CapsulodesisA soft-tissue technique that imbricates or tightens the joint capsule adjacent to the meniscus to indirectly limit extrusion, without direct bony fixation of the meniscus itself.
